Data centers can require new power generation, transmission lines, substations, and other upgrades to the electric grid. This bill would help make sure those costs stay with the large customers that require them instead of being shifted onto families and small businesses. It also includes protections so ratepayers are not left with the bill if a data center later scales back or shuts down.

This is a step in the right direction, but there is more work to do. Data centers also use significant amounts of water and can put additional pressure on local infrastructure. As more of these facilities are built, we need to look at the full impact on the communities where they operate.
